findings.summary: After B15 the log audit still uses start_unix, and nothing binds it. realism places the measure intervals of the offered-load check at start_unix + mono_start and start_unix + mono_end against the event windows (scripts/traffic_log.py:810 and :950). features/qualification.py offered_load places the rows' offered load the same way (:613-634), for the G3a qualification, Z4 and the final evaluation. The log audit checks only that both headers carry the same start_unix (scripts/collection_logs.py:419-420). No check compares any record's t_utc with start_unix + its monotonic time. A start_unix moved in both headers is accepted and can flip offered_load_differs_from_plan either way. B15's own claim holds: the stop no longer depends on start_unix. Honest logs are not affected.

With windows on the two measure intervals that hold two arrivals (14 and 20), placed from the honest start_unix: offered 6, planned 8.933333, ratio 0.671642, ok False. Then I shifted start_unix in both headers and nothing else, by -30, -10, -5, +5, +10, +30 and +5000 s. The ratios are 1.0, 1.041763, 0.983105, 0.99255, 1.051304, 1.0 and 1.0, ok True each time. For every shift, summarize problems are [] and the whole audit_logs problems are []. In the same probe, start_unix moved by -5000, -300, +300 or +5000 s leaves the same 5 sessions out at the stop (share 0.2). Honest logs: over the 74 log pairs of /home/eh/hyptcn3-logs/v5/dokazy/G2/behy, t_utc - (start_unix + t_mono) of the arrivals lies in [-0.0019, +1.5068] ms (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-eh-projects-hyptcn3/9a8a89c1-0c71-4e83-9fec-bd4ea2021d22/scratchpad/g0v5/praca/logs/ends_g2.log).
findings.suggested_fix: This is measurement code, so it belongs to the next package that reopens G0, before offered_load and traffic_realism are judged on G2 sessions. In summarize, refuse a /2 pair whose arrival t_utc, phase-marker t_utc, request t_start_utc or interval t_start_utc differs from start_unix + the record's monotonic time by more than a stated tolerance. For example 1 s, the bound of the nginx correlation; honest drift is below 2 ms. Add a self-test case that moves start_unix in both headers. Until then, the realism docstring and the deviation log should say that the offered load is placed through start_unix and that the audit does not bind it.

findings.summary: requests:end_mono_mismatch binds the request log's end_mono only to the interval log's copy. intervals_not_to_end binds that copy to the last interval's mono_end. That interval lies after the envelope's end D, where planned_sessions is not compared. Nothing compares the stop with the post marker or with the runner's stop. A stop moved later in both end records and in the last interval passes the whole log audit, and the order share returns to B13's stop-biased value. It takes a consistent edit of four fields, and honest logs are not affected.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/-home-eh-projects-hyptcn3/9a8a89c1-0c71-4e83-9fec-bd4ea2021d22/scratchpad/g0v5/praca/skripty/test_sonda_stop3.py (log .../praca/logs/sonda_stop3.log) uses the cut-buyer session of the B14/B15 test (D_max 338, end_mono 748.5, envelope end 720). I moved both end_mono and the last interval's mono_end and duration_s by +1000 or +5000 s; that interval is in phase post. summarize problems are [] in both cases. The share is 4/25 = 0.16 with 0 sessions left out at the stop, against 4/20 = 0.2 with 5 left out as built. Probe .../praca/skripty/test_sonda_stop3b.py (log .../praca/logs/sonda_stop3b.log) uses the clean steady session (with its event) and the clean bursty session. Each is moved by +1000 s the same way and resealed. audit_logs accepts both, with problems [] before and after.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the stop from the other side as well. Either bound end_mono after the post marker's t_mono by what the runner allows, or bound the end record's end_utc against the session's end.json. scripts/collection.py stops the generator right after the measure phase; lab_trial drains longer, so the bound belongs to the session audit. Do it together with the wall-time binding of the first finding, and add a self-test case of the consistent move.

That line is intervals_not_to_end, B3's line, unchanged by B15. The log audit still refuses the session, but as traffic:unreadable and not by the name B15 gives. scripts/lab_trial.py traffic_summary calls summarize without a guard and would raise. In the request log's copy, every non-finite value is refused by name.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/-home-eh-projects-hyptcn3/9a8a89c1-0c71-4e83-9fec-bd4ea2021d22/scratchpad/g0v5/praca/skripty/test_sonda_unreadable.py (log .../praca/logs/sonda_unreadable.log). With the interval copy null, summarize raises TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'float' and 'NoneType'. audit_logs then gives accepted False with problems ['traffic:unreadable:TypeError: ...']. The string '275.5' gives the same. In test_sonda_b15.py::test_probe_end_mono_not_finite, an interval copy of NaN, inf, true or missing gives intervals_not_to_end plus requests:end_mono_mismatch. A request copy of null, NaN, inf, '275.5', true or missing gives requests:end_mono_mismatch, and the order share is null with ok false.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard line 617 with _finite, as the new check does, so that every malformed copy is refused by name. Add one self-test case with a non-numeric interval end_mono, at the next change that reopens G0.
